### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A34, A35, A36 and A37 appear in about 100% of traces, up from about 61%, 61%, 40% and 40% respectively. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A06 appears in about 29% of traces, up from about 7%; A10 appears in about 3% of traces, down from about 10%. [OCC001, OCC002]
- A30 now leads to A34 or A35 in about 99% of its outgoing transitions, whereas before it also led to A36 and A37. [DIR004]
- A34 and A35 now lead to A36 or A37 instead of A31; A31 is no longer a direct successor of either. [DIR005, DIR006]
- A06 is now followed by A16 in about 90% of its outgoing transitions, and A15 now leads to A06 in about 15% of its transitions. [DIR002, DIR003]
- In terms of order, A30 now precedes A34/A35/A36/A37 in almost all cases, and A31 follows them; A34 and A35 precede A36 and A37 in almost all cases. [REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029]
- A06 now appears before A30, A31, A34, A35, A36 and A37 in about 26% of traces, and is often interleaved with A15 and A16. [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL001, REL002]
- The lag between A30 and A31 increased from mostly 3 steps to mostly 5 steps; the lag between A30 and A36/A37 increased from 1–2 steps to 3–4 steps. [LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]
- A06 to A16 now occurs within 1 step in almost all cases. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a hypothesis that, in the later window, the process executes a sequence A30 → A34/A35 → A36/A37 → A31 in nearly all cases, with A06 appearing earlier in about 29% of traces and being followed by A16. This is directly shown by the routing changes (A30 no longer goes to A36/A37, A34/A35 no longer go to A31), the co-occurrence and order relations (A30 before A34/A35/A36/A37, A31 after them, A34/A35 before A36/A37), and the lag distributions (A30–A31 now far apart, A30–A36/A37 later, A06–A16 immediate). The large number of consistent items across multiple indicators makes a chance explanation unlikely. A competing explanation based on sampling differences in variant frequencies cannot be fully excluded, but the coherence of the routing, order and lag evidence strongly favours a structural reordering. Some lag items rest on few observations (e.g., A06–A16 before window had only 5 supporting traces), so the exact placement of A06 relative to the main sequence is less certain. [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG001]
